reason: E1 shows that annealing improves tribocorrosion resistance via a dense oxide layer, supporting the role of oxide stability. E3 shows that microalloying (B) can enhance passive film stability and corrosion resistance, supporting the intervention. However, no cited evidence directly supports the claim that multicomponent mixing enables rapid oxide reformation during sliding, nor the specific prediction linking enhanced oxide stability to reduced wear and ΔOCP in a comparative test. E2 is about a different alloy system and does not address oxide reformation or tribo-corrosion mechanisms.
premises: Multicomponent mixing in HEAs enables rapid reformation of a passive oxide film during sliding.
A stable, adherent passive oxide layer reduces both wear and localized corrosion under tribo-corrosion.
Thermal treatment or microalloying can enhance oxide adhesion and stability.
Enhanced oxide stability leads to lower wear rate, smaller ΔOCP, and less localized corrosion damage.
The dynamic oxide stability mechanism governs total degradation in chloride-rich sliding environments.
